PARTIES This Service Agreement (the Agreement) is made effective on 15 January 2026 (the Effective Date) by and between Northstar Office Systems Pvt. Ltd., a fictional company located in Pune, Maharashtra (Client), and BrightPath Digital Services LLP, a fictional service provider located in Pune, Maharashtra (Provider). The Client and Provider are each a Party and together the Parties. 2. PURPOSE AND SERVICES The Provider will configure and maintain a document-management portal for the Client. Services include initial setup, user training, monthly maintenance, and technical support. Work outside this scope requires a written change request approved by both Parties. 3. TERM AND RENEWAL The Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for twelve (12) months, ending on 14 January 2027, unless terminated earlier under Clause 8. It may be renewed for successive six-month periods if both Parties confirm renewal in writing at least thirty (30) days before

earlier under Clause 8. It may be renewed for successive six-month periods if both Parties confirm renewal in writing at least thirty (30) days before the current term expires. 4. FEES AND PAYMENT The Client will pay a setup fee of INR 75,000 and a recurring service fee of INR 18,000 per month. The Provider will issue an invoice on the first business day of each month. The Client must pay each undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) calendar days of receipt. Overdue undisputed amounts may incur interest at 1% per month, subject to applicable law. 5. OBLIGATIONS OF THE PROVIDER The Provider must: (a) use reasonable skill and care; (b) maintain support availability Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Indian Standard Time, excluding public holidays; (c) notify the Client of a confirmed security incident affecting Client data without undue delay; and (d) provide a monthly service report by the fifth business day of the following month. 6. OBLIGATIONS OF THE CLIENT The Client must provide accurate configuration information, appoint an authorized project contact, and provide access reasonably necessary to perform the services. The Client must review deliverables within seven (7)

an authorized project contact, and provide access reasonably necessary to perform the services. The Client must review deliverables within seven (7) business days and report material defects in writing. Delays caused by missing Client information may extend delivery dates by a reasonable period. 7. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA HANDLING Each Party must protect non-public information received from the other Party and use it only to perform or receive services under this Agreement. These duties do not apply to information that is public through no breach, already lawfully known, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law. On termination, each Party must return or securely delete the other Party's confidential information on written request, except where retention is required by law.

SERVICE AGREEMENT - CONTINUED 8. TERMINATION Either Party may terminate this Agreement for a material breach if the breaching Party fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after written notice. Either Party may terminate for convenience after the first six months by giving sixty (60) days' written notice. Fees for services performed up to the effective termination date remain payable. 9. LIABILITY To the extent permitted by applicable law, neither Party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential loss. Each Party's aggregate liability arising from this Agreement will not exceed the fees paid or payable during the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. This limitation does not apply to fraud, wilful misconduct, or liabilities that cannot lawfully be limited. 10. DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW The Parties will first attempt to resolve a dispute through good-faith discussions between their project leads. If unresolved within fifteen (15) days, the dispute will be escalated to senior management. to senior management. This Agreement is governed by the laws of India, and courts located in Pune, Maharashtra will have jurisdiction, subject to applicable law. 11. An email notice is deemed received when the sender receives no delivery-failure notification and the recipient acknowledges receipt. 12.
